hypotheses.claim: The Harbor St lane closure is making the lunch drive-thru hard to use, so customers give up.
supporting: The drop starts the day the roadworks began
Reviews say the drive-thru queue backs onto Harbor St
counter: A lane closure is not proof customers can't get in
Public data can't show whether lost regulars would come back once it reopens

hypotheses.claim: A rival's $5 lunch deal on Dock Rd is pulling price-sensitive customers away.
supporting: Reddit post mentions switching to the $5 deal
counter: The deal launched on 2 Nov, a week after the drop began

supporting: Two heavy-rain days in the last three weeks
counter: Only 2 days, and every store dipped those days then recovered
The drop is persistent and specific to this store

hypotheses.claim: Local customers are cutting back on eating out.
counter: Area restaurant card spending is flat month on month
Nearby comparison stores are not down the same way

hypotheses.claim: Long lunchtime lines are causing customers to give up.
supporting: Review: "the drive-thru line at noon is brutal now. Gave up."
counter: Reviews are self-selected; we don't know how common this is

unknown: Public data can't tell us why lost regulars actually left, or which single change would bring them back. Price, speed and convenience all look plausible from the outside.

question.text: What would bring you back to Ember Burger on Harbor St for lunch?

rationale: The open suspects map to three concrete levers (a perk, price, speed). One question forces a clear trade-off from people who actually stopped visiting.
